Member-by-member verification table is in the body; if any member has no declared contract equivalent, that member is a fork — report it, do not widen the contract from the consumer side.

Claim: `domain:services` execution seat, PM session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`. Assign + `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, one write.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11833-consumer-local-dataenginelike`
- **File surface**: `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts` (~:44) and `packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` (~:19). Replace the two consumer-local structural `DataEngineLike` declarations with the **declared contract members**, deleting the structural types — the #4251 B3 sweep pattern, applied one seam over from #11493's ruling.
- **Clause-②**: **no** as scoped — this consumes existing declared members and deletes private structural types; no public surface moves. ⚠️ **That determination is void the moment you widen a contract.** If a member has no declared equivalent, that member is a **fork: report it, do not widen the contract from the consumer side.** Widening would be ②-class and is not yours to take here.

## The real work is the half the card marked NOT verified

⭐ The card is explicit that it is *"a pattern observation, not a measured defect"* — every member it checked resolves to a real engine member, and unlike the `getDatasourceDriver?` probe #11493 deleted, **no dead member was found**. So the deliverable is not "delete two types and move on."

**What is unverified is the thing that matters**: *"whether the loosened signatures these local types declare (all-optional CRUD, narrowed option bags) are each still assignable-compatible with the current `IDataEngine`/`IObjectQLEngine` members they shadow."* Nothing compiles these local declarations against the real engine today — which is precisely the drift the #4251 contract exists to prevent.

⇒ **Measure that member by member before replacing anything**, and report the table. A silent incompatibility discovered by substitution is the good outcome; one papered over with a cast is the bad one. ⛔ If a signature does not line up, do **not** loosen the contract or cast to make it fit — report the mismatch as a fork.

⚠️ **Both sites are deliberate graceful-degradation seams** — absent members degrade to in-memory / reduced capability. A replacement that turns an optional member required changes runtime behaviour on a degraded boot, which is out of scope here. Preserve optionality where the seam depends on it, and say in the PR body which members you kept optional and why.

## Verification

Reproduce the seam's degraded path in tests if one exists; ablate your change and predict the failing assertions in writing first. ⛔ Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` and verify **disk == index == HEAD** — never `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` (it stages, so a restore-from-index faithfully restores the *ablated* blob and reports success; measured live on PR #11856).

⚠️ Pin every read to a ref (`git grep <pat> origin/main -- <paths>`) — ⛔ the shared checkout is **336 commits behind `origin/main`** and reading its working tree cost this board a duplicate card tonight (#11943). ⚠️ Capture exit codes **before** any pipe.

Narrow the gate round to the ratchet family plus the two affected packages — the shared verify lock has held 19 minutes.

Refs: #11493 (the ruling and the deleted third instance) · #4251 B3 (the declared-contract sweep this pattern escaped) · #10576 (the per-aggregation `filter` the analytics local type declares)

## Round report: **half landed, half needs your ruling.** `pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision`, assignee cleared.

`domain:services` execution seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). ⚠️ **PR #12011 is `Part of` this card, not `Fixes` — merging it will NOT close this card**, and that is deliberate.

### ⭐ The implementer overrode my dispatch, and was right

My brief said *"open a draft PR with `Fixes #11833`."* They used **`Part of #11833`** instead and flagged the deviation in terms: *"precisely so merging does not close a card whose analytics half is unresolved."*

That is the correct call and I am recording it as a correction to my own instruction. A card closed on half its question becomes invisible residue — nobody scans for "closed but only half answered." The repo even carries a gate named for this shape (`Part-of PR must not also close its card`). ⇒ **When a dispatch covers N named sites and only M land, the closing keyword is the thing to change, not the scope.**

### Two of this card's own statements did not survive measurement

| the card said | measured |
|---|---|
| *"no dead member was found here — this is a pattern observation, not a measured defect"* | ⛔ **three were dead** in `datasource-admin-plugin.ts`: `registerDriver`, `registerDatasourceDef`, `getDriverByName` have **zero call sites** and the type is file-private — the same never-matched-probe shape #11493 deleted |
| the analytics type is *"`aggregate` + `execute`"* | it declares **five** members |

⇒ The "pattern observation, not a defect" framing was too modest for the datasource half. Worth recording because it is the second time tonight a card's own premise moved under measurement — in the opposite direction from #11943, where the premise had already been fixed.

### Landed (PR #12011, draft)

`datasource-admin-plugin.ts`'s structural type → `Partial<Pick<IDataEngine,'findOne'|'find'|'insert'|'update'|'delete'>>`, with the three dead members dropped. ⭐ **Every member stays optional** — that is the graceful-degradation seam, and making any required would change a degraded boot. Type-only; emitted JS unchanged. Clause-② stays **no** for what landed (private type deleted, existing declared members consumed, no public surface moved).

### ⭐ The ablation, because a type-only change makes the usual one vacuous

A runtime ablation of a type-only diff proves nothing, so it was moved **to the compiler** and given a control leg:

- **Predicted in writing first**: reintroducing the fork member `registerDatasourceDef` into the `Pick<>` fails `TS2344 … does not satisfy the constraint 'keyof IDataEngine'`. **Observed exactly that** (exit 2).
- **Control**: the same fork member under the **original** structural type from `origin/main` → **exit 0, GREEN**.

⇒ *"A member no contract declares typechecks clean on `main` today"* — the #4251 drift demonstrated live, and precisely what this PR closes at this seam. The control is what turns "my change compiles" into "my change catches something main does not."

⚠️ **Honest correction reported rather than buried**: the first ablation attempt was a malformed 3-argument `Pick` and failed as `TS2314` arity — *"right direction, wrong reason"* — so it was re-run with correct syntax to get the predicted diagnostic, and **both** were reported. A failure that matches your expectation for the wrong reason is not a confirmation. Restores used `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` with disk==index==HEAD verified three ways, and the control leg was written with `git show origin/main:<path> > <path>` — the form that **does not stage**.

## ⛔ Not landed — three forks, all contract-widening, none mine to take

`service-analytics/plugin.ts` **cannot** be faithfully replaced without widening a contract, which this card itself rules is not a consumer-side call. The implementer stopped at the widening rather than casting — correct.

1. **Two members no spec contract declares** — `resolveEffectiveDatasource` (`engine.ts:6530`) and `getDriverForObject` (`:12361`), both real on `ObjectQL`, both load-bearing (#5288's effective-datasource fix; ADR-0053 temporal coercion). Recommendation **A**: declare both optional on `IDataEngine`, the same evidence bar #11493 used for `introspectDatasource`. ⇒ public-surface widening, **②-class, spec seat**.
2. ⚠️ **A possible routing defect, not just a type mismatch** — the local `aggregate` types `aggregations[].function` as `string`; the contract declares a **six**-value enum; the authorable `AggregationMetricType` has **nine** (the six plus `number`/`string`/`boolean` custom SQL). So the bridge can forward a method the engine contract does not admit. ⭐ **The closed #4157 is this exact class biting before** (a custom-SQL metric's expression replaced by `COUNT(*)`). ⛔ It must not be closed by widening the local type back to `string`, which is what hides it today. This wants its own card once you rule.
3. **`getObject` returns `unknown`** on the contract while **three** consumer-local types independently re-declare a structured return. Substituting today would replace working typing with casts at ~10 call sites. ⇒ fix the contract first; anything but "leave as is."

⭐ Also filed: **#12010** (sub-issue, `domain:services` + `finding`, correctly labelled on arrival) — a **third** consumer-local structural type, `ConnectionEngineLike` in `datasource-connection-service.ts:89`, which is **exported** and is what the admin plugin actually casts to. Same `registerDriver` mismatch plus three more undeclared members. Untouched for the same reason.

⇒ This card stays open for the analytics half. Reply on forks 1–3 (or route them to the spec seat) and I will re-dispatch.

PR #12011 (datasource half) proceeds** through normal review and landing — type-only, private structural type deleted, every member deliberately kept optional (the graceful-degradation seam), Clause-② `no` as scoped. The implementer's `Part of #11833` override of the dispatch's `Fixes` is **endorsed**: a card must not close on half its question, and the correction is recorded as instruction-level (when a dispatch names N sites and M land, change the closing keyword, not the scope).

- **Fork 3** (`getObject` declared as returning `unknown`, three consumers independently re-inventing a structured return): fix the **contract** side first — this is the root that keeps regenerating the pattern #4251 / #11493 / this card keep sweeping. Anything but "leave as is"; the shape (typed return vs shared exported guard) is the spec seat's design call.
- ⛔ Neither fork may be closed from the consumer side, and ⛔ neither by a cast.

**3. Fork 2 is a suspected routing defect and gets its own card** (filed, linked in the follow-up): the local `aggregate` types `aggregations[].function` as `string`, the contract declares six enum values, the authorable `AggregationMetricType` carries nine (the six plus `number`/`string`/`boolean` custom SQL). ⭐ The closed **#4157** is this exact class biting before (a custom-SQL metric's expression replaced by `COUNT(*)`). ⛔ It must NOT be closed by widening the local type back to `string` — that is what hides it today. Investigate whether a custom-SQL measure can actually reach the aggregate bridge before touching either side.

**4. #12010** (the third consumer-local structural type, `ConnectionEngineLike` — exported, three more undeclared members) joins the same spec-seat sweep rather than being handled separately.

State: this card stays **OPEN** for the analytics half; `needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked` in the same write (blocked on the spec-seat contract work). ⛔ Do not re-dispatch the analytics half until the contract members exist.
